text:
**Review Result**

Score: **5.5/10**. The repo is small and readable, and the existing happy-path tests pass, but I would not approve it as-is. The biggest problems are URL path construction, loose API response validation, and pagination/batch behavior that can fail badly in edge cases.

I verified with:

`PYTHONPATH=/tmp/lumen-review-deps:. PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/lumen-pycache python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`

Result: **9 passed**.

**Findings**

| Severity | File | Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| high | `lumen/client.py` | 171-172, 193-196, 224, 239-242 | Resource IDs are interpolated directly into URL paths without percent-encoding, allowing `/`, `..`, `?`, or `#` to change the requested endpoint. |
| high | `lumen/client.py` | 158-169, 219-230 | Pagination only stops on `next_cursor is None`, so an API returning `""` or a repeated cursor can loop forever. |
| medium | `lumen/client.py` | 164-166, 198-200, 225-227 | Malformed response items/results are silently skipped instead of raising an API contract error, causing invisible data loss. |
| medium | `lumen/client.py` | 185-191 | `batch_create` eagerly materializes the entire iterable, contradicting “any iterable/any number” behavior and risking memory blowups. |
| medium | `lumen/models.py` | 54, 97, 142, 160 | `Literal`-typed enum fields are not validated at runtime, so invalid server states like `"deleted"` are accepted. |
| medium | `lumen/models.py` | 29 | `bool(data.get("retryable"))` treats string values like `"false"` as `True`, which can trigger retries for non-retryable errors. |
| medium | `lumen/client.py` | 77-91 | Transport errors and timeouts are not wrapped in `LumenAPIError`, so callers must handle raw `httpx` exceptions despite the typed-error API. |
| low | `lumen/client.py` | 232-243 | Review requests always send `"note": null` when omitted; APIs that distinguish omitted fields from null may reject or misinterpret the request. |
| low | `lumen/models.py` | 40-56, 59-82, 85-103, 106-126 | Frozen dataclasses contain mutable dictionaries without defensive copies on direct construction, so model instances are not truly immutable. |
| low | `README.md` | 87-100 | Documentation says `batch_create` handles “any number” of tasks, but implementation loads all tasks into memory before chunking. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **180 lines**. That includes URL encoding helpers and tests, stricter response/model validation, safer pagination termination, streaming batch chunking, exception wrapping, and docs updates.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this PR as-is.**

issues.description: Resource IDs are interpolated directly into URL paths without percent-encoding, allowing path/query manipulation.
Pagination only stops on null cursors, so empty or repeated cursors can cause infinite loops.
Malformed response items/results are silently skipped instead of raising an API contract error.
batch_create eagerly materializes the entire iterable before chunking, risking high memory usage.
Literal-typed status/verdict fields are not validated at runtime, so invalid API values are accepted.
retryable parsing uses bool(), so string values like "false" become true.
Transport errors and timeouts are not wrapped in the package's typed exception hierarchy.
Review requests send note as null when omitted instead of omitting the field.
Frozen dataclasses expose mutable dictionary fields without defensive copying on direct construction.
Documentation claims batch_create supports any number of tasks, but implementation loads all tasks into memory.
